units.text: EXT. FLOODED BELL FOUNDRY - DAWN
A broken roof, a pit of cold black water, and a great cracked bell lying on its side half-submerged.
Smoke from a burning village drifts over the ridge.
Rifle fire somewhere a long way off.
CORPORAL AUGUSTIN LEFEBVRE, twenties, French, mud to the knees, wades along the edge of the pit with his rifle held high.
He stops.
Across the water, on the far lip of the bell, a figure is crouched, equally muddy, equally still: PRIVATE ANSELM WEBER, twenties, German, a bandage on his forearm.
They raise their rifles at the same moment.
Neither fires.
Tu es seul?
units.name: LEFEBVRE

units.text: Allein.
units.name: WEBER

units.text: A beat.
The water between them ripples in the wind.
Put it down.
units.name: LEFEBVRE

units.text: You first.
units.name: WEBER

units.text: No.
units.name: LEFEBVRE

units.text: Weber's finger moves on the trigger.
Lefebvre's does too.
A bird takes off from the broken roof and both of them flinch, and the rifles drop an inch.
They stay there.
Weber's eyes go to the bell.
It's cracked.
units.name: WEBER

units.text: It was cracked before.
units.name: LEFEBVRE

units.text: Weber lowers his rifle, slowly, and sets it on the curve of the bell.
He holds up his hands.
Lefebvre watches him, wades one step closer, then two.
At three steps, the far wall of the foundry collapses with a roar.
Both men dive.
Lefebvre lands on the bell, Weber lands on him, and for a moment they are two shapes thrashing in the churned water, fists and elbows, a rifle sinking, a helmet floating away.
Lefebvre gets an arm around Weber's neck.
Weber bites his wrist.
They both scream.
A shell lands in the village beyond the ridge, and the whole pit shudders.
They freeze.
Both of them, still tangled, looking at the sky.
That's ours.
units.name: WEBER

units.text: That's ours.
units.name: LEFEBVRE

units.text: Slowly, they let go of one another.
Weber retrieves his helmet from the water.
Lefebvre wipes his bleeding wrist on his sleeve.
There's a road past the bell. Go.
units.name: LEFEBVRE

units.text: Why?
units.name: WEBER

units.text: Lefebvre shrugs.
He picks up his rifle and does not point it.
Weber waits, then wades out of the pit, climbing the ridge in the smoke.
Halfway up, he turns, lifts one hand.
Lefebvre does not lift his.
He sits down heavily on the bell and takes out a cigarette that is too wet to light.
